question: Can a verifier-coupled neural program synthesizer bootstrap from random programs and finite OEIS prefixes, continually expanding a population of short or fast symbolic explanations without training on human-written programs?

key_findings.claim: A search-check-learn loop grows a self-generated training corpus from random initialization to tens of thousands of OEIS prefix-matching programs.
key_findings.evidence: Each iteration decodes up to 240 candidate programs for every one of 351,663 sequences, executes candidates, also matches their outputs against an OEIS prefix tree, retains the shortest and fastest match for each sequence, and retrains sequence-to-program translation. The longest run reports 78,118 solved entries after 190 iterations; all runs together reached 84,587 by January 2023.

key_findings.claim: The synthesized objects are executable and interpretable, but a finite-prefix match is not automatically a mathematical explanation.
key_findings.evidence: Programs use a human-designed Turing-complete two-variable DSL with arithmetic, conditionals, primitive-recursive loops, paired-state loops, and unbounded minimization. Verification accepts generation of the available finite OEIS terms under time and magnitude limits; distinct functions can share that prefix, and some successful programs exploit numerical approximations rather than the intended formula.

key_findings.claim: Replacing tree-guided MCTS with an attentive LSTM translator and wide beam search substantially raises coverage, but the comparison changes compute and several mechanisms.
key_findings.evidence: The 500-iteration tree-neural baseline plateaus near 45,000 solutions, the basic NMT run reaches 46,707 in 100 iterations, and the extended NMT run exceeds 78,000 by iteration 190. NMT evaluates 84.4 million raw candidates per single-model iteration and later twice that, while the baseline uses a different search and candidate budget, so the curves are not a controlled algorithm-efficiency comparison.

key_findings.claim: Model portfolios and continued training sustain discovery, while the checker itself accounts for the largest visible one-step gain.
key_findings.evidence: Adding a half-data specialist at iteration 21 produces 687 new solutions versus 272 in the basic run. Continuous training begins at iteration 70, a quarter-data specialist at 156, slow checking at 159, and a larger model at 170. Switching from hybrid to slow checking jumps new solutions from 178 to 860, confounding claims that persistent discovery comes primarily from learned search.

key_findings.claim: Dual selection for program length and execution cost supports continual symbolic improvement.
key_findings.evidence: The checker keeps both a shortest and fastest program, and later learners propagate replacements through the population. Over 100 iterations following initial discovery, average retained size and abstract execution cost decline; the 24 successive prime predicates and their population frequencies provide a concrete evolutionary trace. Single-objective 20-iteration ablations slightly outperform the joint objective, so long-run synergy remains inferred rather than isolated.

key_findings.claim: Short programs extrapolate better than fast programs among candidates that finish, but timeout-inclusive coverage is much lower than the headline percentages.
key_findings.evidence: Of 40,577 solved entries with 100 extra b-file terms, 14,701 shortest and 11,056 fastest programs time out. Among finishers, 90.57% of shortest and 77.51% of fastest programs match all extra terms; relative to all 40,577 entries, those are only about 57.8% and 56.4% respectively before accounting for any semantic mismatch with the intended OEIS definition.

anchors.section: Generalization of the solutions to larger indices

key_findings.claim: The system rediscovers reusable low-level algorithms, but automatic macro induction is not shown to improve coverage.
key_findings.evidence: Detailed cases include more than twenty prime predicates, a triangular pairing code that packs two logical values into one DSL variable, and numerous linear upper bounds for decoding it. Local and global macro runs initially look strong because they start portfolios and slow checking earlier; each adds fewer than 2,800 entries beyond the main run and remains below 100 iterations, so library-learning benefits are inconclusive.

key_findings.claim: The project is a useful result archive but not an end-to-end reproducible release.
key_findings.evidence: The linked GitHub repository at commit 753bbbe stores hundreds of per-iteration logs, selected generated programs, macro statistics, and human analyses. It contains no synthesizer/checker/training source, environment specification, license, test suite, checkpoints, or runnable reconstruction of the three-month experiment; its only Python artifacts are example programs.

method.core_idea: Turn every OEIS prefix into a source sequence for neural translation, decode compact DSL programs, verify them by execution, use hindsight matching against all prefixes, retain Pareto-style shortest and fastest winners, and repeatedly retrain on the growing set of machine-discovered pairs.
method.mechanism: Exact execution supplies dense, non-human labels after rare successful searches. Those verified programs shift the translator toward useful token patterns; wide beam search and heterogeneous model portfolios recombine them, while length and abstract runtime pressure gradually favor compact and reusable algorithms.
assumptions: Matching the available OEIS prefix is a useful proxy for discovering its generating rule.
The hand-built DSL contains compact expressions for a meaningful fraction of OEIS.
Shorter or faster matching programs are more likely to reflect the intended rule.
Abstract execution cost approximates useful machine efficiency consistently.
Self-generated training examples do not lock the search into a narrow local language.
OEIS targets and b-files are uncontaminated by the model because training starts without human programs.

techniques.role: Alternates proposal, exact execution, winner selection, and retraining.
Matches every generated trace against all OEIS sequences as hindsight replay.
Provides executable arithmetic, loops, search, and paired state in prefix notation.
Produces 240 high-probability program candidates per target and model.
Combines full-data, subset-specialist, continuous, and larger translators.
Retains both minimum-token and minimum-runtime programs.
Escalates promising prefixes under larger execution and comprehension limits.
Tests local definitions and globally frequent action subsequences.

evaluations.setting: All 351,663 OEIS entries available in March 2022, 190 extended NMT iterations
evaluations.metric: Cumulative entries with at least one finite-prefix-matching program and new matches per iteration
evaluations.result: The main run reaches 78,118 entries and continues adding mostly hundreds per late iteration; all runs together reach 84,587.
evaluations.baseline: The authors' 500-iteration tree-neural/MCTS continuation and 100-iteration single-NMT run

evaluations.metric: Number of solved prefixes under embedding, DSL, and fitness variants
evaluations.result: Local search offsets larger-model cost; the default/extra combined language and single-objective selection perform best in this short regime.
evaluations.baseline: Default 64-dimensional tree model, base DSL, and dual fitness

evaluations.setting: Late extended-run model portfolio over iterations 175-186
evaluations.metric: Unique candidates, own solved entries, and newly added entries
evaluations.result: The quarter-data 512-unit specialist generally beats the 1024-unit continuous model and undertrained base model because it produces more diverse candidates under the budget.
evaluations.baseline: Continuous half-data model paired with each alternative

evaluations.setting: 40,577 solved OEIS entries with 100-term b-file continuations
evaluations.result: 90.57% of non-timeout shortest programs and 77.51% of non-timeout fastest programs agree; timeout-inclusive rates are about 57.8% and 56.4%.

limitations: Finite-prefix agreement is underdetermined and does not prove the intended mathematical definition.
The headline solution count treats every prefix match as solved and does not incorporate extrapolation or proof.
Only a subset has b-files, and the published extrapolation percentage excludes large timeout groups.
The system is not free of human bias: DSL, fitness, timeouts, search, targets, and architecture are all designed.
The extended run changes portfolio, training regime, sequence lengths, checker, model size, and compute at different iterations without controlled replication.
Candidate counts and wall-clock budgets differ across tree and NMT comparisons.
Macro experiments are incomplete and do not establish learned abstraction as a causal advantage.
A three-month, roughly 1.8-MWh main run receives no seed-level uncertainty or compute-normalized comparison.
The public repository preserves outputs and logs but omits executable training/checker code, tests, environment, license, and checkpoints.
failure_modes: A spurious finite-prefix program passes verification but diverges immediately after recorded terms.
A correct compact program times out and is counted as a failure while an approximate shortcut survives.
The DSL cannot express the intended rule compactly, so search rewards an unrelated enumerator.
Self-training amplifies early syntactic motifs and reduces behavioral diversity despite more candidates.
Hindsight matching finds a different OEIS prefix collision and misattributes the candidate's target.
Changing abstract operator costs changes which program becomes a training winner.
A slower checker, not a smarter generator, accounts for apparent late learning progress.
Global macros become frequent-token compression rather than semantically reusable concepts.
Program text is interpretable syntactically but too convoluted for a mathematician to validate semantically.
reusable_insights: Pair generative models with deterministic evaluators whenever candidates are cheaply executable.
Use hindsight matching to convert every candidate trace into feedback for all compatible targets.
Keep multiple winners for distinct objectives instead of collapsing size and runtime into one arbitrary scalar.
Measure extrapolation on hidden terms and count timeouts in the denominator.
Distinguish prefix satisfaction, functional extrapolation, semantic intent, and formal proof as separate validation levels.
Normalize search comparisons by unique candidates, evaluator time, accelerators, and wall-clock budget.
Ablate evaluator strength independently because verification budget can dominate generator gains.
Track lineage of discovered subprograms to diagnose population convergence and reusable innovation.
Release the checker, DSL interpreter, training orchestration, exact configs, and frozen data snapshot with result archives.
open_questions: Can formal recurrence induction or theorem proving certify that a synthesized program matches an OEIS definition for all indices?
What verifier schedule maximizes new valid rules per joule rather than raw prefix matches?
Can behaviorally diverse archives prevent self-training collapse better than random data specialists?
Do typed, automatically invented libraries improve search once evaluated under matched compute?
How much coverage comes from genuinely new algorithms versus recombinations of a few common arithmetic schemas?
Can a learned timeout/value model preserve slow correct programs without exploding evaluator cost?
How should ambiguity be scored when several simple programs extrapolate but embody different mathematics?
Can contemporary code models improve discovery without importing human OEIS solutions from pretraining?
Would co-evolving tests and programs expose prefix overfitting earlier?
Can the loop transfer learned abstractions to conjecturing, proof search, or environment generation?

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Program Synthesis for Integer Sequences from Scratch
competitive_landscape.difference: Gauthier and Urban introduce the same from-scratch OEIS feedback loop with tree-neural policy guidance and MCTS, reaching 27,987 matches. Alien Coding's main additions are NMT beam decoding, dual fitness, model portfolios, longer evolution, and exploratory macros.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Symbolic Regression for Recurrent Sequences
competitive_landscape.difference: d'Ascoli et al. supervise Transformers on synthetic formulas to infer analytic recurrence relations and evaluate a selected OEIS test set. Alien Coding avoids human/synthetic formula supervision and searches a more expressive executable DSL over all entries, but has weaker semantic and test-split guarantees.

competitive_landscape.title: DreamCoder: Growing generalizable, interpretable knowledge with wake-sleep Bayesian program learning
competitive_landscape.difference: DreamCoder jointly compresses learned solutions into reusable symbolic abstractions and trains recognition models across several domains. Alien Coding scales a simpler verifier loop across OEIS, while its local/global macro experiments do not yet demonstrate the abstraction gains central to DreamCoder.

competitive_landscape.title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
competitive_landscape.difference: FunSearch evolves LLM-generated code in diverse islands and surpasses best-known cap-set and bin-packing results under explicit evaluators. It uses pretrained human code and problem skeletons but validates novelty against established optima, whereas Alien Coding starts without human programs yet mostly validates finite known prefixes.

competitive_landscape.title: Progressive Self-Learning for Domain Adaptation on Symbolic Regression of Integer Sequences
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhu et al. combine target-conditioned synthetic source data with NMT, beam verification, and progressive self-learning to reduce the synthetic-to-OEIS distribution gap and report state-of-the-art formula accuracy. It is more directly evaluation-oriented, while Alien Coding explores a broader Turing-complete program space from random seeds.

competitive_landscape.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: AlphaEvolve uses multiple pretrained LLMs, asynchronous evolutionary populations, and task evaluators to improve algorithms and scientific constructions, including verified state-of-the-art results. Alien Coding provides an earlier fully self-generated learner in a tiny DSL but lacks AlphaEvolve's open-ended standard-code editing and achievement-based validation.

competitive_landscape.title: CodeEvolve: An open source evolutionary coding agent for algorithm discovery and optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: CodeEvolve exposes an island-based, LLM-guided evolutionary stack with crossover and meta-prompting and benchmarks against AlphaEvolve-style tasks. Its reproducible framework and diversity controls address major artifact gaps in Alien Coding, though it relies on pretrained code knowledge.

competitive_landscape.title: IntSeqBERT: Learning Arithmetic Structure in OEIS via Modulo-Spectrum Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: IntSeqBERT predicts held-out integers with magnitude and modular streams plus CRT reconstruction, reporting explicit train/test next-term metrics. It does not produce interpretable programs, but its held-out protocol cleanly measures arithmetic extrapolation that Alien Coding's headline prefix coverage obscures.

novelty_assessment: Alien Coding is an unusually large and well-instrumented early example of verifier-driven self-training in which the learned proposal distribution and symbolic population co-evolve without human program demonstrations. Its 78,118-entry coverage, dual speed/length lineage, and triangular-coding case are substantive engineering observations. The strongest scientific caveat is that 'solution' means finite-prefix agreement under a human-designed DSL and timeout, not proof or semantic recovery; timeout-inclusive hidden-term success is about 56-58%. DreamCoder already established learned library bootstrapping, and concurrent recurrent symbolic regression offered cleaner test accuracy. Later FunSearch, AlphaEvolve, CodeEvolve, and direct progressive OEIS self-learning add stronger population diversity, pretrained generative priors, reproducible systems, or achievement/test-based validation. The most valuable future direction is to combine this paper's uncontaminated verifier loop with explicit held-out, formal, diversity, and compute-normalized gates.
reviewer_notes: Read all 36 cached pages, including the complete DSL semantics, checker/timeouts, every training intervention, energy accounting, extrapolation denominator, triangular-pairing derivation and generated Python, 24 prime programs and their population tables, and the 123-entry qualitative sample. Visually inspected the loop, encoding, ablation table, portfolio curves, generalization panel, size/runtime evolution, pairing bounds, code listings, lineage grids, and appendix examples. Audited the public repository's current main commit 753bbbe72fc4a88009a18bcb9b1cd3ac9cc363ab: 857 files are overwhelmingly logs/results/explanations, with no runnable system source, tests, environment, license, or checkpoints. Checked direct OEIS synthesis, DreamCoder, FunSearch, progressive self-learning, AlphaEvolve, CodeEvolve, and current OEIS prediction primary sources through 2026-08-23.
